sources.title: High altitude cruise
sources.text:
Above 10,000 ft the physiological environment becomes the limiting
factor. Time of useful consciousness falls from around 20 minutes at
18,000 ft to well under a minute above 35,000 ft.

Hypoxia is dangerous because its onset is comfortable: euphoria, poor
judgement and slowed reaction arrive before any sense of breathlessness.
The victim often feels fine.

Know the aircraft's oxygen or pressurisation system and check it before
departure rather than when needed. In a pressurisation failure, the
sequence is oxygen mask on first, then an emergency descent, then
communicate.

Cruise altitude selection trades against wind. A higher level offers
lower fuel flow and better true airspeed, but the jet stream can impose a
headwind that outweighs both. The winds-aloft forecast decides which
level is fastest.

sources.title: Density altitude
sources.text:
Density altitude is pressure altitude corrected for temperature, and it
is what the aircraft actually feels. High elevation, high temperature and
high humidity each reduce air density, and their effects combine.

Consequences are simultaneous and all unfavourable: the engine produces
less power, the propeller is less efficient, and the wing needs a higher
true airspeed for the same lift. Takeoff roll lengthens, climb rate falls
and the service ceiling drops.

An airfield at 5,000 ft on a hot afternoon can behave like 8,000 ft or
more. Performance charts assume a standard atmosphere, so the correction
is not optional.

Plan departures for early morning where possible, reduce weight rather
than hope, and compute the actual takeoff distance for the actual
conditions against the actual runway length.

sources.title: Engine failure in flight
sources.text:
The order is fixed: fly the aircraft, pick a field, then troubleshoot.
Pilots have flown serviceable aircraft into the ground while working a
checklist.

Establish best glide speed immediately and trim for it. Best glide is a
specific number for the aircraft and weight, and both faster and slower
reduce the distance available.

Choose a landing site while altitude still offers a choice, favouring
into-wind, long, smooth and unobstructed over merely close. Commit early;
changing target late costs more than the imperfection of the first
choice.

Then run the restart flow: fuel selector to a tank with fuel, mixture
rich, carburettor heat on, ignition on both, boost pump as fitted.

Declare an emergency. Squawk 7700. Secure fuel and ignition before touch
down, keep the shoulder harness tight, and fly the aircraft all the way
into the crash.

sources.title: Emergency descent
sources.text:
An emergency descent is warranted by pressurisation failure, an
uncontrolled fire, or any condition where remaining at altitude is more
dangerous than descending rapidly.

With a pressurisation failure the order is oxygen first. Consciousness is
the prerequisite for everything else, and time of useful consciousness at
high altitude is measured in seconds.

Then descend at the maximum rate the airframe allows: power to idle,
speed brakes as fitted, and a bank to increase the rate while keeping the
speed within limits. In turbulence or with suspected structural damage,
use a lower speed -- a rapid descent that overstresses the airframe has
solved nothing.

Level off at a safe altitude. 10,000 ft is standard where terrain allows,
and the minimum safe altitude for the sector where it does not.

Declare the emergency and squawk 7700.
